headline: Democrats sweep Congress: dollar hits one-month low, oil sinks 9%, pound and franc lead
summary: The dollar index fell about 0.2% to near 101.6 after touching 101.21, its lowest since Sept 30, as the Democrats' sweep of Congress pulled Treasury yields down and trimmed Fed hike bets; a beat in ADP payrolls and a 3% Dow rally limited the drop. The Aussie, franc, pound and euro led with gains of about 0.4–0.55%, while the Taiwan dollar and peso slipped on local pressures and the yen gave back most of an early 0.8% rally.
drivers: Democrats took both the House and Senate, which markets read as fiscal gridlock and tougher AI regulation. The 10-year Treasury yield fell to about 4.91%, Fed hikes priced to June 2027 dropped about 3bp to 55bp, and the euro touched 1.1272, its highest since Oct 6.
Oil collapses on Iran peace hopes

Brent fell 8.7% to $94.62 and WTI 8.3% to $88.12 after the administration tied the Iran war to the defeat, raising hopes of an end to the conflict. Even so, the loonie hit a seven-week high near 1.3930, and the rupee firmed to 94.64.

Foreigners sold a net NT$149.9bn of Taiwan shares and 2.5tn won of Korean shares, so the Taiwan dollar fell to a fresh 1.5-year low of 32.821 and the won barely moved at 1,341.5 despite the weaker dollar.
view: Mildly bearish for the next 1–2 weeks: a Democratic Congress, lower Treasury yields and cheaper oil all chip at the dollar, though ISM prices paid at 73 and Fed hike pricing should stop a rout. I sell dollar rallies against the yen near 159 and against the loonie, but back it against the Taiwan dollar while foreigners keep selling Taiwan stocks. A DXY close above 102.50 after payrolls would make me neutral; a close below 101.20 opens 100.50.
ideas: Hold the short from 1.4030–1.4050, about 0.5% in favour, with the stop trailed to 1.4020; for 1.3850 as the US dollar weakens.
Buy 32.70–32.78 as record foreign selling of Taiwan stocks overwhelms the central bank's smoothing; for 33.10, stop 32.55.
Sell 158.80–159.20 into Tokyo's intervention zone as US yields ease; for 157.00, stop 160.30.
review: Neither the USD/JPY sale at 159.20–159.50 nor the USD/TWD buy at 32.65–32.75 filled (the day's extremes were 158.75 and 32.781), so both stay open at adjusted entries. USD/CAD's short is about 0.5% in favour, USD/IDR's long slightly in favour and the ringgit sale back to about flat; GBP/USD and EUR/JPY closed above their range tops, so both ranges move higher.

eurusd.note: Up about 0.4% to 1.1233 after a one-month high at 1.1272; just under the 1.1250 range top.
eurusd.why: The dollar did the moving. Democrats won both chambers of Congress, which markets read as fiscal gridlock and tougher scrutiny of AI, so the 10-year Treasury yield fell to about 4.91% and Fed hike pricing out to June 2027 slipped about 3bp to 55bp. The euro hit its best level since Oct 6 before a 3% Dow rally and a solid ADP report trimmed the gain.
eurusd.outlook: I lift the range to 1.1150–1.1300 and buy dips: lower US yields and cheaper oil help Europe, but the Fed is still priced to hike. A close above 1.1300 would open 1.1400.
eurusd.watch: US jobless claims (Nov 5), US payrolls (Nov 6), US-Iran talks and oil.

view.call: 1.1150–1.1300; buy dips as US yields ease.

gbpusd.note: Up about 0.45% to 1.3473, closing above the 1.3450 range top before Thursday's BoE.
gbpusd.why: Both sides helped. The dollar fell on the Democratic sweep and lower Treasury yields, while sterling is supported by a near-certain Bank of England hike to 4% on Thursday, the first since 2023, with swaps pricing about four hikes over the next year. That left the pound among the day's leaders.
gbpusd.outlook: I raise the range to 1.3380–1.3560 rather than chase: with so much priced, a 6–3 vote or pushback on market pricing would knock the pound back, while an 8–1 vote and hawkish guidance would open 1.3600.
gbpusd.watch: BoE decision, vote split and guidance (Nov 5), US payrolls (Nov 6).

view.call: 1.3380–1.3560; BoE vote split is the swing.

audusd.note: Up about 0.55% to 0.7003, back above 0.70 after a 12-day low at 0.6954.
audusd.why: The dollar did the moving. The Aussie first lagged as AI stocks slid in Asia, then rebounded once the Democratic sweep pushed Treasury yields lower and Wall Street rallied about 1.6% on the S&P 500. It is still digesting Tuesday's dovish RBA hike to 4.85%, where a 6–3 vote and dropped tightening bias capped rate support.
audusd.outlook: I keep a 0.6950–0.7060 range: the best carry in G10 and a softer dollar support dips, but the 100- and 200-day averages near 0.7030–0.7060 cap rallies. A close above 0.7060 would open 0.7120.
audusd.watch: China trade data, US payrolls (Nov 6), iron ore, AI-stock sentiment.

usdjpy.note: Down about 0.15% to 158.41 after a low at 157.39; the yen gave back most of its early gain.
usdjpy.why: The yen first jumped about 0.8% as haven demand and a drop in the 10-year Treasury yield to about 4.89% followed the Democratic sweep. It then faded as global stocks rallied and US ADP payrolls beat at 86,000 against 69,000 expected, which eased the need for havens. Tokyo's warnings that it will act on disorderly moves kept buyers cautious near 158.75.
usdjpy.outlook: I keep selling rallies but lower the entry to 158.80–159.20, just above the day's high, for 157.00: falling US yields and Tokyo's 159–160 line limit the upside. A close above 160.30 would end the call.
usdjpy.watch: Tokyo intervention talk, Japan wage data, US jobless claims (Nov 5) and payrolls (Nov 6).

view.call: Sell 158.80–159.20; Tokyo's 160 line, US yields easing.

usdchf.note: Down about 0.5% to 0.8166 after a low near 0.8133; the 0.8150 floor held on the close.
usdchf.why: The franc did most of the moving. It was the top haven pick as early results showed a Democratic sweep, rising almost 1% in Asia, and kept about half of that as Treasury yields fell. Tuesday's jump in Swiss inflation to 1.5%, the highest in almost three years, also makes the SNB less keen to lean against a stronger franc.
usdchf.outlook: I lower the range to 0.8130–0.8280: haven demand and a softer dollar favour the franc, but crowded longs and possible SNB selling should slow it. A daily close below 0.8130 would open 0.8050.
usdchf.watch: Weekly sight deposits (Nov 9), SNB speakers, US payrolls (Nov 6).

usdcad.note: Down about 0.25% to 1.3972 after 1.3930, the loonie's best since Sept 16; the short is in favour.
usdcad.why: The US dollar did the moving. The Democratic sweep knocked the greenback broadly, and a wider Canadian trade surplus added support. The loonie held its gains even as oil collapsed, with WTI down 8.3% to $88.12 after the administration tied the Iran war to the election loss, and Canada's 10-year yield fell about 4bp.
usdcad.outlook: I keep the short for 1.3850, about 0.5% in favour, and trail the stop to 1.4020: a weaker US dollar and trade hopes outweigh oil for now. A further oil slide or weak Canadian jobs would be the risks.
usdcad.watch: Canada jobs and US payrolls (Nov 6), oil and US-Iran talks, BoC speakers.

view.call: Short from 1.4030–1.4050; weak USD, wider trade surplus.

usdcnh.note: Little changed near 6.675, at a two-week low for the yuan after another weak PBOC fixing.
usdcnh.why: Beijing did the moving. The PBOC set its midpoint at 6.7180, its weakest since Oct 23 and 369 pips weaker than the Reuters estimate of 6.6811, a day after announcing a rise in the FX reserve ratio to 6% from Nov 15. That offset the broad dollar slide and a 2% rally in Shanghai stocks, so the yuan barely gained.
usdcnh.outlook: I keep a 6.64–6.70 range: the PBOC is now slowing the yuan's rise, but a weaker dollar and steady exporter conversion limit any drop. A close above 6.70 would show Beijing wants more weakness.
usdcnh.watch: Daily fixings vs estimates, China trade data, FX reserve ratio rise (Nov 15).

view.call: 6.64–6.70; PBOC slowing the yuan, dollar soft.

usdhkd.note: Little changed near 7.845, still near the 7.85 weak edge of the peg.
usdhkd.why: Nothing local moved the pair. A wide gap between US and Hong Kong rates keeps carry traders selling Hong Kong dollars, which holds it near 7.85, where the HKMA would buy them. A 1.7% rise in the Hang Seng and the broad dollar slide made little difference.
usdhkd.outlook: No trade in 7.83–7.85: the carry gap pins it near 7.85, and only a sharp rise in HIBOR or HKMA buying would pull it lower.
usdhkd.watch: HKMA operations at 7.85, HIBOR, US payrolls (Nov 6).

view.call: 7.83–7.85, no trade; carry gap keeps it near 7.85.

usdsgd.note: Down about 0.2% to near 1.279, back in the middle of its range as the dollar slid.
usdsgd.why: The dollar did the moving. The Democratic sweep and lower Treasury yields lifted Asian currencies in early trade, and the Singapore dollar followed with the euro. Gains were modest because the yuan was held back by another weak PBOC fixing and the Taiwan dollar fell on heavy foreign stock selling.
usdsgd.outlook: I keep the 1.2740–1.2860 range: a strong S$NEER path and a softer dollar favour the lower half, while regional outflows limit gains. A close below 1.2740 would open 1.2700.
usdsgd.watch: US payrolls (Nov 6), China trade data, foreign flows from Asian tech stocks.

usdkrw.note: Won eased 0.5 to 1,341.5 at the Seoul close after a 1,336.1–1,347.2 range.
usdkrw.why: The won stood still while flows pulled both ways. The dollar fell broadly and Korean three-year bond yields dropped to about 3.70%, but foreigners sold a net 2.5tn won of Kospi shares, taking November selling to about 4.4tn won, and local dollar demand absorbed the gains. The Kospi swung more than 400 points before closing up 0.6%.
usdkrw.outlook: I keep the 1,330–1,355 range: heavy foreign selling limits won gains, while a softer dollar and exporters cap the upside. A close above 1,355 would point to 1,370.
usdkrw.watch: Foreign Kospi flows, US payrolls (Nov 6), AI-chip sentiment.

usdtwd.note: Taiwan dollar fell 6.1 cents to 32.821, a fresh 1.5-year closing low; high 32.900.
usdtwd.why: Equity outflows did the moving again. Foreigners sold a net NT$149.9bn of Taiwan shares, even more than Tuesday's NT$107bn, as the Taiex fell as much as 3.1% before closing down 0.8%. Governor Yang told lawmakers the currency's 3% fall this year comes from foreigners cashing in stock gains, so the broad dollar slide did little to help it.
usdtwd.outlook: I stay long: record outflows are overwhelming the central bank's smoothing. The 32.65–32.75 entry did not fill, so I buy 32.70–32.78 for 33.10; a close below 32.55 would end the call.
usdtwd.watch: Foreign Taiex flows, TSMC October sales (Nov 10), US payrolls (Nov 6).

view.call: Long 32.70–32.78; record foreign selling of Taiwan stocks.

usdmyr.note: Ringgit rose to 4.0610/0660 at the 6pm close from 4.0735/0775, ahead of Bank Negara.
usdmyr.why: The dollar did the moving. The Democratic sweep pushed the dollar index down about 0.5% during Kuala Lumpur hours, and the ringgit gained against the dollar and most Asean peers. Gains were held back by caution before Bank Negara's Nov 5 decision, which research houses expect to leave the OPR at 2.75%.
usdmyr.outlook: I hold the sale for 4.010, now roughly at entry: a softer dollar should resume the ringgit's rally once Bank Negara is out of the way. A close above 4.085 would end the call.
usdmyr.watch: Bank Negara decision (Nov 5), US payrolls (Nov 6), regional chip stocks.

view.call: Sold 4.055–4.065; soft dollar, BNM Nov 5 the swing.

usdphp.note: Peso slipped 6.5 centavos to 63.535 before October inflation data.
usdphp.why: The peso did the moving. Traders cut exposure before Thursday's October CPI, which the BSP sees at 7.1–8.1% after 7.2% in September, as higher fuel, power and transport costs raise stagflation worries. The 8.7% slide in Brent to $94.62 came after Manila's close and should help on Thursday.
usdphp.outlook: I keep the 63.30–64.20 range: much cheaper oil and BSP smoothing support the peso, but high inflation and weak growth keep the 64.17 record low in view. A close below 63.30 would open 63.00.
usdphp.watch: Philippine October CPI (Nov 5), BSP comments, oil, US payrolls (Nov 6).

view.call: 63.30–64.20; oil relief vs CPI risk, BSP smooths.

usdidr.note: Rupiah eased 8 points to 18,168 (Bloomberg); the JISDOR rate firmed to 18,140.
usdidr.why: The rupiah slipped on its own side. It opened about 0.25% stronger at 18,115 as the dollar fell, but foreign selling and caution before Thursday's Q3 GDP data pulled it back. Bank Indonesia's Destry Damayanti said the bank will keep intervening to steady the currency, which is down about 7.9% this year.
usdidr.outlook: I keep the long for 18,300, slightly in favour, on outflows and policy doubts; I would add on dips to 18,100–18,130. A close below 18,060 would end the call.
usdidr.watch: Indonesia Q3 GDP (Nov 5), Bank Indonesia operations, foreign bond flows.

usdinr.note: Rupee firmed to 94.64 from 94.74, a fourth daily gain, after a two-week high early on.
usdinr.why: The rupee gained as the dollar index fell about 0.4% in Mumbai hours and oil eased, with foreign inflows adding support. Importers and banks bid for dollars near 94.50, where the RBI is also seen buying to rebuild reserves, so the gains faded. Brent's later 8.7% plunge to $94.62 cuts India's import bill.
usdinr.outlook: I lower the range to 94.20–95.20: much cheaper oil favours the rupee, but the RBI caps gains by buying dollars on dips. A Brent close back above $105 would push it toward 95.20.
usdinr.watch: Oil and US-Iran talks, RBI dollar buying, US payrolls (Nov 6).

view.call: 94.20–95.20; cheaper oil vs RBI dip buying.

eurjpy.note: Up about 0.2% to near 177.9, closing just above the 177.8 range top.
eurjpy.why: The euro did the moving. It gained about 0.4% against a weaker dollar after the Democratic sweep, while the yen's early haven rally faded as stocks surged. That pushed the cross just through 177.8, though Tokyo's warnings keep a lid on yen weakness.
eurjpy.outlook: I raise the range to 176.5–179.0 but would not chase: Tokyo is likely to lean against further yen weakness, and a softer dollar helps the yen too. A close above 179 would open 180.
eurjpy.watch: Tokyo intervention talk, Japan wage data, ECB speakers.

cnhjpy.note: Down about 0.2% to near 23.73 as the yen edged up and the yuan held steady.
cnhjpy.why: The yen did the moving. It gained slightly against the dollar after the Democratic sweep, while the yuan barely moved because the PBOC's weaker-than-expected fixing at 6.7180 held it back. That left the cross in the middle of its range.
cnhjpy.outlook: I keep the 23.3–23.9 range: Beijing is slowing the yuan and Tokyo is guarding the yen, so neither leg has room to run.
cnhjpy.watch: PBOC fixings, FX reserve ratio rise (Nov 15), Tokyo intervention talk.

watch: Next: the BoE (a hike to 4% expected), Bank Negara, Philippine CPI, Indonesia GDP and US jobless claims (Nov 5), US payrolls and Canada jobs (Nov 6), TSMC sales (Nov 10) and the PBOC's FX reserve hike (Nov 15), plus Tokyo's 159–160 line and US-Iran talks.
